brief.description: A broad oak textile bench with an upright open loom frame, copper roller and integrated front controller.
brief.purpose: Make wool-to-cloth production recognizable as a skilled town craft and visually distinct from the wet brick tannery.
brief.silhouette: Three blocks wide and three deep: low wide workbench in front, two narrow rear loom uprights, one top beam and one horizontal roller across an open center.
brief.bounds: Controller at front-center; assembly stays within x=-1..1, depth=0..2 and no more than four blocks high.
brief.materials: Vanilla/resource-pack oak construction, restrained copper roller/bearings and a pale woven swatch on the controller face.
brief.interfaces: Existing front-center controller, contextual guide, coal processing and inventory behavior remain unchanged.
brief.states: Static structure; controller retains existing working/fire state behavior and shared UI.
brief.construction: Existing planks, copper and saw-cut slabs/beams/eighth cubes; no new decorative block, banner or entity.
brief.invariants: No recipe, production, capacity, fuel or inventory changes. No required wool construction block or invented powered mechanism.
brief.technological_stage: Organized town artisan workshop built from frontier timber and simple metal fittings.
brief.material_behavior: Directional oak grain, pale woven controller insert and warm copper only at the roller/bearings.
brief.signature_feature: Open upright loom frame above a broad low workbench with one copper roller.
brief.neighboring_assets: Tannery, Smithy, Cloth and Raw Hide.
fidelity_targets: Workbench reads two to three blocks wide and about one block high with visible legs and a thin top.
Two narrow loom posts and top beam frame a large open center.
One horizontal copper roller has visible support at both ends.
Controller is integrated into the front bench and shows a pale woven swatch.

references.role: Frozen assembly and exact Minecraft material/scale context; the revised Textile Workshop is in the middle.
Project multiblock presentation and partial-block construction language only.
Woven material identity and pale cloth/blue accent language only.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: implementable Minecraft multiblock design reference
Primary request: Redesign the Civilization Textile Workshop as one coherent, attractive late-nineteenth-century loom and workbench assembly.
Input images: Image 1 is the current in-game workshop lineup and material/scale context; redesign only the middle Textile Workshop. Image 2 is presentation and partial-block construction language only. Image 3 is woven material identity only.
Subject: A three-block-wide, three-block-deep textile workstation with the controller at bottom front center. Make a low broad oak workbench with a thin slab top and four short partial-block legs. At the rear, two narrow oak loom uprights support one top crossbar around a large open center. One horizontal copper roller spans the frame with visible bearings. Integrate a small pale woven swatch with restrained blue selvage into the controller face at the front; do not invent a separate cloth block.
Style/medium: polished Minecraft build mockup using feasible full blocks, slabs, quarter beams and eighth cubes; 32x resource-pack material density; late nineteenth-century artisan workshop.
Composition/framing: side-by-side front three-quarter and rear three-quarter views of the same isolated assembly on a neutral stone floor, matching scale and orientation.
Materials/textures: warm oak, restrained copper roller/bearings, small dark iron controller fittings, pale wool swatch with one narrow blue edge.
Constraints: exact maximum footprint 3x3 blocks, maximum height 4 blocks, controller at front-center, Minecraft half-block geometry, broad negative space, buildable with existing oak/copper cut pieces. No separate cloth panel in the structure.
Avoid: solid plank cube, full-block fence-like posts, spinning-wheel complexity, decorative gears, belts, pipes, modern machinery, floating thread, people, labels, impossible curves, tiny clutter.
